title: Platform Administration Portal (Staff Guide)
content:
# Platform Administration Portal (Staff Guide)
This section is for **Omni Platform staff** (the people who run the platform itself), not for customers. It explains the separate **Platform Admin Portal** (also shown on screen as "Omni Platform Staff Portal" / "Governance Portal"). Customers never see this portal and use their own workspace app instead.

Everything in this section is based on how the portal actually behaves today. Where a screen label and the real behaviour differ, a **Notes** line explains the difference.

## Contents of this section

1. Portal overview and the Privacy Shield
2. Staff roles and what each role can open
3. Signing in, signing out, and session behaviour
4. Navigating the portal (sidebar, header, role-based landing page)
5. Tenant Workspaces
6. SaaS Plan Tiers
7. Subscriptions
8. Payments and Invoices
9. Support Helpdesk
10. Infra Telemetry
11. System Logs
12. Testing Suite
13. Staff and RBAC
14. Platform Audit Trail
15. Common tasks (quick recipes)
16. Common errors and fixes
17. Glossary

---

title: Portal overview and the Privacy Shield
content:
# Portal overview and the Privacy Shield
## 1.1 What the portal is for

The Platform Admin Portal lets authorised Omni Platform employees:

- See a catalogue of customer workspaces (called **tenants**) and their plan, usage and limits.
- Create and edit **plan tiers** (pricing and limits).
- Manage each workspace's **subscription** (plan, status, expiry date, limits) and renew it.
- Record **payments** and issue **invoice numbers**.
- Answer customer **support tickets**.
- Watch the health of the platform servers, read system logs, and run simple test tools.
- Manage the platform staff accounts themselves.
- Review a permanent **audit trail** of staff actions.

## 1.2 The Privacy Shield (data-blind rule)

The portal is deliberately **data-blind**. A green banner "Strict Data Privacy Shield Guarantee" appears on several screens, and a small green pill "Data Privacy Shield: Zero-PII Active" is always visible in the sidebar (on phones, at the top of the sidebar). The banner also shows a lock tag "Zero Impersonation Policy".

What this means in practice:

| Staff CAN see | Staff CANNOT see |
|---|---|
| Workspace name, ID, plan, plan status, expiry date | Customer conversations or message text |
| Counts: channels, staff seats, messages this month, contacts count | Customer contact lists or personal details |
| Plan limits and usage bars | Customer orders, products or payment card details |
| Subscription and invoice ledger entries (invoice number, amount, method, reference, notes) | Knowledge bases, AI documents or uploaded files |
| Support tickets and the messages customers deliberately send to support | Any way to "log in as" a customer |

Key points:

- **There is no impersonation.** The portal has no "log in as this customer" or "view workspace as owner" feature. The banner states a "Zero Impersonation Policy". Staff sign-in tokens are also different from customer tokens, and customer tokens are rejected by the portal.
- Tenant screens show **counts and totals only**, never customer content.
- The payment ledger holds a **record** of payments (amount, method, reference). It does not hold bank card numbers or other card credentials.
- System logs are described on screen as "Zero-PII compliant". Treat logs as confidential operational data anyway.
- Support tickets are the one place where customer-written text appears, because the customer chose to send it to support. Treat ticket content as confidential.
- Every important change you make is written to the **Platform Audit Trail** under your staff identity (see section 14).

> **Good to know:** ** The Privacy Shield is a policy and design guarantee built into which data the portal can read. It is not a switch you can turn on or off from the screens.

---

title: Staff roles and what each role can open
content:
# Staff roles and what each role can open
There are four staff roles. Every staff account has exactly one role. The role is shown as a coloured badge in the sidebar.

| Role (shown as) | Internal name | Colour | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Super Admin | `super_admin` | Purple | Full governance: plans, billing changes, tenant limits, staff accounts, everything else |
| Platform Dev | `platform_dev` | Cyan | Server telemetry, logs, test tools |
| QA / Tester | `platform_tester` | Amber | Test tools only |
| Support Agent | `support_agent` | Green | Helpdesk, subscriptions, payments, tenant lookup, logs, audit trail |

## 2.1 Screen access by role

"Yes" means the item appears in the sidebar and opens. If a role types the address of a screen it is not allowed to open, it sees the "Platform Access Restricted" page (see 3.5).

| Screen (sidebar name) | Super Admin | Platform Dev | QA / Tester | Support Agent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tenant Workspaces | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| SaaS Plan Tiers | Yes | No | No | No |
| Subscriptions | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Payments & Invoices | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Support Helpdesk | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Infra Telemetry | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| System Logs | Yes | Yes | No | Yes |
| Testing Suite | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Staff & RBAC | Yes | No | No | No |
| Platform Audit Trail | Yes | Yes | No | Yes |

## 2.2 Action permissions inside screens

Some screens open for several roles, but certain buttons are for fewer roles. The portal hides the button, and the server also refuses the action if someone tries it another way.

| Action | Super Admin | Platform Dev | QA / Tester | Support Agent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Create / edit / delete or deactivate a plan tier | Yes | No | No | No |
| "Govern" button on a tenant (edit plan, status, limits) | Yes | No | No | No |
| Edit a subscription (pencil icon) | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Quick Renew a subscription | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Record Payment Entry (button on Payments screen) | Yes | No | No | No (see note) |
| View payment ledger | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Reply to tickets, add internal notes, change status/priority/assignee | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Create staff, change staff role/status | Yes | No | No | No |
| View the staff list (the list itself) | Yes | No | No | No (see 9.9) |
| Clear log buffer / download log files | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| Open the Error Stack Traces tab | Yes | Yes | No | Yes |
| Dispatch a synthetic (test) webhook | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Run the Channel Health Audit | Yes | Yes | Yes | No (no screen) |

> **Good to know:** **
- For **Record Payment Entry**, the server would accept a Support Agent, but the portal only shows the button to Super Admins. Plan on Super Admin doing manual payment entries. Support Agents can record a payment by using **Quick Renew** on the Subscriptions screen, which also creates an invoice entry (see section 7.7).
- There is no per-person fine-grained permission editor in the portal. Access is decided entirely by the role.

---

title: Signing in, signing out, and session behaviour
content:
# Signing in, signing out, and session behaviour
## 3.1 How to get there

Open the Platform Admin Portal address given to you by your administrator (it is a different address from the customer app). If you are not signed in you are taken to **Omni Platform Staff Portal – Internal Infrastructure & Governance Gateway**.

## 3.2 Sign-in fields

| Field | Required | Details |
|---|---|---|
| Platform Staff Email | Yes | Your internal staff email address. Must be a valid email format. Not case-sensitive. Spaces at the start/end are removed. |
| Staff Password | Yes | Use the eye icon to show or hide the password. |
| MFA Code (Optional for dev) | No | Up to 6 characters, placeholder "6-digit TOTP token". |
| Sign In to Platform Admin (button) | - | Shows "Authenticating Staff..." while working. |

> **Good to know:** **
- The MFA Code box is shown, but the current sign-in process does **not** check it. You can leave it empty. The "MFA Enforced / Standard Auth" label on the staff list simply reflects a stored flag on the account.
- The sign-in page has no "Forgot password" link and no "Sign up" link. Staff accounts are created only by a Super Admin (section 13).

## 3.3 Step-by-step: sign in

1. Open the portal address.
2. Type your **Platform Staff Email**.
3. Type your **Staff Password**.
4. Leave **MFA Code** blank (or type it if your administrator told you to).
5. Click **Sign In to Platform Admin**.
6. You land on your role's starting screen (see 4.3). If you were sent to the sign-in page after trying to open a particular screen, you are returned to that screen after signing in.

## 3.4 Sign-in messages and what they mean

| Message | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| "Email and password are required" | One of the two fields was empty | Fill in both fields |
| "Invalid platform credentials" | Email not found, or password wrong (the same message is used for both on purpose) | Re-type carefully; ask a Super Admin to confirm your account exists |
| "Platform staff account is suspended. Access denied." | A Super Admin set your account to Suspended | Contact a Super Admin |
| "Platform staff account is deactivated. Access denied." | Your access was terminated | Contact a Super Admin |
| "Invalid platform staff credentials" | Generic fallback if the server gives no detail | Try again, then contact an administrator |

## 3.5 Session behaviour

- Your session lasts **24 hours** by default (the platform operator can change this), after which you must sign in again.
- Each time a screen loads, the portal re-checks that your account is still **Active**. If a Super Admin suspends or deactivates you, the portal stops accepting your requests ("Platform staff account is suspended. Access denied.").
- If your session has expired or is invalid, you are signed out automatically and sent to the sign-in page.
- **Sign Out Session** (bottom of the sidebar) ends your session on that browser and takes you to the sign-in page.
- Customer (tenant) accounts cannot sign in here. Their tokens are rejected.

## 3.6 "Platform Access Restricted" page

If you open a screen your role is not allowed to use, you see a red shield icon, the heading **Platform Access Restricted**, and the text "Your platform role (xxx) does not have sufficient clearance to access this governance module." Click **Return to Permitted View** to go back one page in your browser history.

## 3.7 Changing your own password or display name

The server supports changing your own display name and password (new password must be at least **10 characters** and you must supply your current password). However, **the portal currently has no screen for this**. Ask your administrator how this is handled in your organisation.

---

title: Navigating the portal
content:
# Navigating the portal
## 4.1 Layout

- **Left sidebar** (top of the page on phones):
  - Brand block: "Omni Platform / Governance Portal".
  - **Your identity card**: first letter avatar, your name, your email, your role badge, and a pulsing "ONLINE" marker.
  - **Navigation links**: only the screens your role may use. Each link has a small tag (for example "Zero-PII", "Pricing", "Lifecycle", "Ledger", "Cases", "Live", "Stream", "QA").
  - The Privacy Shield pill.
  - **Sign Out Session** button.
- **Top bar**: "Internal Clearance / <current screen name>" and a green pill "API Gateway Connected".
- **Main area**: the current screen.

## 4.2 Sidebar links and tags

| Link | Tag | Opens |
|---|---|---|
| Tenant Workspaces | Zero-PII | Section 5 |
| SaaS Plan Tiers | Pricing | Section 6 |
| Subscriptions | Lifecycle | Section 7 |
| Payments & Invoices | Ledger | Section 8 |
| Support Helpdesk | Cases | Section 9 |
| Infra Telemetry | Live | Section 10 |
| System Logs | Stream | Section 11 |
| Testing Suite | QA | Section 12 |
| Staff & RBAC | (none) | Section 13 |
| Platform Audit Trail | (none) | Section 14 |

## 4.3 Where you land after signing in

| Role | Landing screen |
|---|---|
| Super Admin | Tenant Workspaces |
| Support Agent | Tenant Workspaces |
| Platform Dev | Infra Telemetry |
| QA / Tester | Testing Suite |

Typing an unknown address takes you back to your landing screen.

## 4.4 Standard screen behaviours (apply to most screens)

- **Search boxes**: type and press **Enter** to search. The page number returns to 1.
- **Dropdown filters**: take effect immediately when changed and return to page 1.
- **Refresh button** (circular arrows icon): reloads the current data.
- **Pagination**: **Previous** / **Next** buttons with "Page X of Y". A button is greyed out at the first/last page.
- **Pop-up forms (modals)**: close with the **X** at the top right or **Cancel**. Red error banners at the top of a form explain why a save failed.
- **Times and dates** are shown in your browser's local time zone and date format.

---

title: Tenant Workspaces
content:
# Tenant Workspaces
## 5.1 Purpose

A data-blind catalogue of every customer workspace: plan, status, channel usage, seat usage and monthly message usage. Super Admins can also adjust a workspace's plan, status, expiry and limits from here.

## 5.2 How to get there and who can use it

Sidebar > **Tenant Workspaces**. Allowed roles: **Super Admin, Support Agent**. Support Agents see the catalogue read-only (no Governance column).

## 5.3 Screen layout

1. Privacy Shield banner.
2. Title "Tenant Workspaces Catalog" and the **Refresh** button.
3. Six summary cards.
4. Search and filter bar.
5. The workspace table and pagination.
6. (Super Admin) the "Override Entitlements & Lifecycle" pop-up.

## 5.4 Summary cards

| Card | Meaning |
|---|---|
| TOTAL TENANTS | Number of workspaces on the platform |
| ACTIVE WORKSPACES | Workspaces whose status is Active |
| TRIAL WORKSPACES | Workspaces whose status is Trial |
| SUSPENDED | Workspaces whose status is Suspended |
| ACTIVE CHANNELS | Connected, active channels across all workspaces |
| PLATFORM STAFF | Number of staff accounts (all roles and statuses) |

## 5.5 Search and filters

| Control | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Search box ("Search by Tenant ID, name, or slug...") | Matches part of the workspace name or its ID. (Despite the hint, "slug" searching is not supported.) |
| Plans dropdown | "All Plans" or one plan (lists every plan, including inactive ones). Filters on the plan the workspace is on. |
| Statuses dropdown | All Statuses, Active, Trial, Suspended, Cancelled |

## 5.6 Table columns

| Column | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Tenant / Workspace | Workspace name and its ID |
| Plan & Status | The plan's display name and a status badge (see 5.7) |
| Connected Channels | "active channels / maximum channels" |
| Staff Users | "number of users / seat allowance" (see note) |
| Monthly Messages | Messages counted since the start of the current calendar month, "/ monthly limit", and a progress bar. The bar turns **red above 90%** of the limit. |
| Created Date | When the workspace was created |
| Governance (Super Admin only) | **Govern** button |

Ten workspaces per page. Footer: "Showing N of M workspaces".

> **Good to know:** **
- The seat allowance in "Staff Users" is estimated from the plan name: enterprise = 100, growth = 25, starter = 10, anything else = 5. It is **informational** and is not an editable limit.
- "Monthly Messages" counts all messages recorded for the workspace this calendar month.

## 5.7 Status badges

| Badge | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ACTIVE (green) | Workspace is in good standing |
| TRIAL (amber) | Workspace is on a trial |
| SUSPENDED (red) | Staff have suspended the workspace |
| Other (grey, e.g. CANCELLED, EXPIRED) | Shown in capital letters as stored |

## 5.8 "Govern" pop-up: Override Entitlements & Lifecycle (Super Admin)

Opened from the **Govern** button. While it opens, the portal loads the workspace's current subscription so that fields show current values. The **Save Entitlements** button stays disabled until loading finishes.

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Plan Tier | Dropdown of all plans. If the workspace is on a plan code that no longer exists, that code is still listed so nothing is lost. |
| Status | Active, Trial, Suspended, Cancelled, Expired |
| Expiration Date | Date picker. **Leave blank for lifetime** (no expiry). |
| Max Channels | Whole number, required |
| Max Contacts | Whole number, required |
| Messages / mo | Whole number, required |
| AI Queries / mo | Whole number, required |

A reminder inside the pop-up says changes are recorded in the audit logs under your staff ID.

Server rules applied to the four limits (values below the minimum are raised to the minimum automatically):

| Limit | Minimum accepted |
|---|---|
| Max Channels | 1 |
| Max Contacts | 10 |
| Messages / mo | 100 |
| AI Queries / mo | 0 |

> **Good to know:** **
- The pop-up text says "-1 for unlimited". In the current server logic, a value of -1 is **raised to the minimum** (for example Max Channels becomes 1), not stored as unlimited. Do not use -1 to mean unlimited. Enter a very large number instead if you need an effectively unlimited allowance, and confirm the result on the Subscriptions screen afterwards.
- Changing the **Plan Tier** in this pop-up does **not** automatically reset the four limits to the new plan's values, because the pop-up always sends the numbers shown in the form. If you want the new plan's standard limits, type them in (see the plan card on the SaaS Plan Tiers screen) before saving.

## 5.9 Step-by-step: change a workspace's plan, status or limits (Super Admin)

1. Open **Tenant Workspaces**.
2. Find the workspace (search by name or paste its ID).
3. Click **Govern** on its row.
4. Wait for the fields to fill in with current values.
5. Change **Plan Tier**, **Status**, **Expiration Date** and/or limits.
6. Click **Save Entitlements**. The button shows "Saving...".
7. On success the pop-up closes and the table and summary cards refresh.
8. If a red message appears, read it, fix the field, and save again (see 5.11).

## 5.10 Step-by-step: suspend a workspace

1. Open **Tenant Workspaces** and click **Govern** on the workspace.
2. Set **Status** to **Suspended**.
3. Click **Save Entitlements**.
4. The SUSPENDED card at the top increases by one, and the row shows a red SUSPENDED badge.
5. To restore, repeat and set **Status** to **Active** (and set a correct expiry date if needed).
6. The action appears in the Audit Trail as `subscription.lifecycle_update` (see the note below).

> **Good to know:** **
- The Govern pop-up uses the subscription update service, so the audit entry recorded is `subscription.lifecycle_update` (not `tenant.governance_update`).

## 5.11 Common errors on this screen

| Message | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Tenant workspace not found" / "Tenant with ID ... not found" | The workspace was removed or the ID is wrong | Refresh and pick the workspace again |
| "Insufficient platform permissions..." | Your role is not Super Admin/Support Agent | Ask a Super Admin |
| "Failed to update tenant governance" | General failure | Try again; if repeated, check Infra Telemetry and System Logs |
| Table says "No workspaces matched the current search filter." | Nothing matches | Clear the search and filters |
| Table list stays on "Loading workspace metadata..." | Server unreachable | Refresh, check Infra Telemetry |

---

title: SaaS Plan Tiers
content:
# SaaS Plan Tiers
## 6.1 Purpose

Define the pricing tiers customers can be placed on: price, currency, usage limits, marketing features list, badge text, and visibility.

## 6.2 How to get there and who can use it

Sidebar > **SaaS Plan Tiers** (tag "Pricing"). Allowed role: **Super Admin only**.

## 6.3 Screen layout

- Header "SaaS Subscription Plans".
- Controls: **Show Inactive Tiers** checkbox (on by default), a **Refresh Plans** icon, and **Create Plan Tier**.
- A grid of plan cards (cheapest first).
- Create / Edit pop-up.

## 6.4 Plan card contents

| Item | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Name and optional badge | Display name plus badge text such as "Popular" |
| ID | The permanent plan code |
| ACTIVE / INACTIVE | Inactive cards are dimmed |
| Description | Short text |
| Price | "<currency> <monthly>/mo" and "or <currency> <yearly>/yr" |
| "Publicly Visible" tag | Shown when the plan is public |
| "Enterprise Custom" tag | Shown when the plan is marked custom |
| Entitlement Quotas | Max Channels, Max Contacts, Messages / mo, AI Queries / mo. Shows "Unlimited" if the stored value is -1. |
| Included Features | First five features, then "+ N more features" |
| **Edit Tier** and trash icon | Edit; Deactivate or Delete |

Plans that exist on a fresh platform (these can be edited): Free Sandbox (`free`), Starter Growth (`starter`), Pro Scale (`pro`), Enterprise Custom (`enterprise`).

## 6.5 Create / Edit form fields

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| Plan Code Identifier | Yes (create only) | Letters, numbers, dash and underscore. Capitals become lower-case. Other characters are replaced or removed. Must be unique. **Cannot be changed later** (greyed out when editing). Examples: starter, pro, enterprise |
| Display Name | Yes | Text |
| Description | No | One line |
| Price Monthly | Yes | Number, 0 or more, up to 2 decimals |
| Price Yearly | Yes | Number, 0 or more, up to 2 decimals |
| Currency | No | Typed in capitals automatically; default USD |
| Max Channels | Yes | Whole number, minimum 1 |
| Max Contacts | Yes | Whole number, minimum 10 |
| Messages / mo | Yes | Whole number, minimum 100 |
| AI Queries / mo | Yes | Whole number, minimum 0 |
| Badge Text (Optional) | No | E.g. "Most Popular" |
| Features List | No | One feature per line. Empty lines are dropped |
| Active Tier | Toggle | "Available for workspaces" |
| Public Pricing | Toggle | "Visible in catalog" |
| Custom / Enterprise | Toggle | "Manual assignment" |

Defaults when you open Create: monthly 29, yearly 290, USD, channels 5, contacts 5000, messages 25000, AI queries 1000, four sample features, Active and Public ticked.

Values lower than the minimum are raised to the minimum automatically (for example a Max Contacts of 5 is saved as 10).

> **Good to know:** **
- The form says "-1 for unlimited", but the server raises -1 up to the minimum on both create and edit. Do not rely on -1 for new or edited plans. Plans seeded with -1 (if any) display "Unlimited".
- "Price Yearly" is required on the form. The server default (if it were blank) is ten times the monthly price.
- Editing a plan changes **the plan definition**. It does **not** change limits already stored on existing workspaces. Use Subscriptions or Tenant Workspaces to change a given workspace.

## 6.6 Step-by-step: create a plan tier

1. Open **SaaS Plan Tiers**.
2. Click **Create Plan Tier**.
3. Enter a **Plan Code Identifier** (for example `agency`).
4. Enter **Display Name**, prices, currency and the four limits.
5. Optional: badge text, description, features (one per line).
6. Set the toggles for Active, Public, Custom.
7. Click **Create Plan Tier** ("Saving Plan..." shows).
8. The card appears in the grid. The action is audited as `plan.create`.

## 6.7 Step-by-step: edit a plan tier

1. Click **Edit Tier** on the card.
2. Change fields (the code is locked).
3. Click **Save Plan Changes**. Audited as `plan.update`.

## 6.8 Step-by-step: retire a plan (deactivate or delete)

1. Click the **trash** icon on the card.
2. Confirm the question "Are you sure you want to deactivate or delete plan tier ...?"
3. The portal then shows one of two results:
   - If **no workspace** uses the plan: it is **deleted** permanently ("Plan '...' successfully removed.").
   - If **any workspace** uses it: it is **deactivated and hidden from public**, not deleted ("... is currently assigned to N workspace(s). It has been deactivated and hidden from public selection instead of deleted.").
4. Audited as `plan.delete` or `plan.deactivate`.
5. To bring a deactivated plan back, click **Edit Tier** and tick **Active Tier** (and **Public Pricing** if wanted).

## 6.9 Common errors

| Message | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "id, name, and priceMonthly are required" | A required field was empty | Fill the missing field |
| "Plan slug ID is required (e.g. starter, pro, enterprise)" | Code was empty or had only unsupported characters | Use letters/numbers/dash/underscore |
| "A plan with ID 'x' already exists." | Code already used | Choose another code |
| "Invalid plan identifier..." | Code contained nothing valid | Use a valid code |
| "Plan 'x' not found." | Plan was removed meanwhile | Refresh |
| "No SaaS subscription plans found..." | None exist or all inactive with checkbox off | Tick **Show Inactive Tiers** or create one |

---

title: Subscriptions
content:
# Subscriptions
## 7.1 Purpose

Manage each workspace's subscription lifecycle: see plan, status, expiry and limits; renew it with a recorded payment; or manually override plan, status, expiry and limits.

## 7.2 How to get there and who can use it

Sidebar > **Subscriptions** (tag "Lifecycle"). Allowed roles: **Super Admin, Support Agent** (both can renew and edit).

## 7.3 Search and filters

| Control | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Search ("Search by workspace name or tenant ID...") | Part of the workspace name or ID. Press Enter |
| Statuses | All Statuses, Active, Trial, Expired, Suspended, Cancelled |
| Plans | All Plans or one plan |
| Refresh icon | Reloads |

Ten rows per page.

## 7.4 Table columns

| Column | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Workspace | Name and workspace ID |
| Current Plan | Plan name and plan code |
| Status & Expiry | Status badge and expiry date with days left, or "No Expiry (Lifetime)" |
| Entitlements (Channels/Msgs) | "Channels: active / max" ("∞" if -1), "Msgs: limit/mo", "AI: limit/mo" ("Unlimited" if -1) |
| Last Payment | Date of the last recorded payment and its invoice number ("Direct Renew" if no invoice number), or "No payment record" |
| Actions | **Quick Renew** button and a pencil icon (Edit lifecycle & quotas) |

## 7.5 Status badges and days-left colours

| Badge | Meaning |
|---|---|
| ACTIVE (green) | In good standing |
| TRIAL (amber) | Trial period |
| SUSPENDED (red) | Suspended by staff |
| EXPIRED (red) | Shown when status is Expired **or** the expiry date has passed, even if the stored status still says Active |
| Other text | e.g. cancelled, shown as stored |

Days-left text next to the date: green when more than 7 days, amber when 7 or fewer, red "Expired" when the date has passed.

## 7.6 Subscription statuses explained

| Status | Meaning | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| active | Paid up and running | Renewal or payment entry sets it automatically; staff can set it |
| trial | Trial period | Staff |
| suspended | Paused by staff (for example for non-payment or abuse) | Staff |
| cancelled | Customer ended or staff ended the subscription | Staff |
| expired | Subscription period ended | Staff; also displayed automatically when the expiry date passes |

> **Good to know:** ** The system does not automatically change the stored status to "expired" when the date passes. The badge shows EXPIRED based on the date, but the stored status remains until staff or a renewal changes it.

## 7.7 Quick Renew

Quick Renew records a **paid** payment for the workspace, creates an invoice number, and sets the workspace to **Active** with a new expiry date.

Pop-up title "Renew Workspace Subscription".

| Field | Required | Details |
|---|---|---|
| Subscription Plan Tier | Yes | Lists plans with their monthly and yearly price. Defaults to the workspace's current plan. Picking a plan fills the Amount with that plan's price for the chosen cycle |
| Billing Cycle | - | "Monthly (+30 Days)" or "Yearly (+365 Days)". Changing it refills the Amount |
| Amount Paid ($) | Yes | Number 0 or more, up to 2 decimals. You can edit the suggested figure |
| Payment Method | - | Stripe, Razorpay, Direct Bank Wire / Transfer, Corporate Credit Card, Manual Admin Override / Cash, Cryptocurrency (default Stripe) |
| Payment Notes / Ref | No | Free text. Pre-filled with "Workspace renewal for <name>". Use it for wire or receipt references |
| Dispatch transactional email receipt & invoice to workspace owner | Checkbox, on by default | Sends a receipt email to the workspace owner's email address, if the workspace has an owner |
| Confirm & Renew Subscription | Button | Shows "Renewing..." |

What the renewal does:

- Records a payment with status **paid** and a new invoice number (format `INV-YYYYMM-NNNN-XXXX`).
- Sets the subscription period to **start now** and end one month (monthly) or one year (yearly) later.
- Sets the workspace plan to the chosen plan, status to **Active**, expiry to the new end date, and **resets all four limits to the chosen plan's standard values**. Any custom limits you set earlier are overwritten.
- Sends the receipt email if ticked (a failure to email does not cancel the renewal).
- Is recorded in the Audit Trail as `subscription.renew`, naming the invoice number, amount, plan and workspace.

> **Good to know:** **
- The new period always starts **today**; it is not added on top of days remaining. Renewing a workspace that still has time left can therefore **shorten** its expiry. For a different period, use **Record Payment Entry** (section 8) with a specific duration, or edit the expiry date manually.
- The Amount field is labelled with "$" even if the plan currency differs. The renewal itself is recorded in USD.
- Month and year are calendar months/years even though the labels say +30 and +365 days.

## 7.8 Step-by-step: renew a subscription

1. Open **Subscriptions**.
2. Search for the workspace.
3. Click **Quick Renew** on its row.
4. Check the **Subscription Plan Tier** and **Billing Cycle**.
5. Check that **Amount Paid** matches what the customer actually paid.
6. Choose the **Payment Method**.
7. Put the bank or receipt reference in **Payment Notes / Ref**.
8. Keep or clear the receipt email checkbox.
9. Click **Confirm & Renew Subscription**.
10. The row now shows ACTIVE, the new expiry, and the new invoice number under Last Payment.

## 7.9 Edit lifecycle and quotas (pencil icon)

Pop-up title "Override Entitlements & Lifecycle". Fields are the same as the Govern pop-up in section 5.8: Plan Tier, Status (Active, Trial, Suspended, Cancelled, Expired), Expiration Date (blank = lifetime), and the four limits. The same minimums and the same cautions about "-1" and about plan changes not resetting limits apply. Button: **Save Entitlements** ("Saving...").

Audit entry: `subscription.lifecycle_update`.

## 7.10 Step-by-step: extend a trial or set an expiry date

1. Click the pencil icon on the workspace row.
2. Set **Status** to Trial (or Active).
3. Choose a new **Expiration Date**.
4. Click **Save Entitlements**.

Expiry dates are stored as the start of the chosen day (UTC), so the exact moment may differ slightly by time zone.

## 7.11 Common errors

| Message | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "planId and amount are required to record renewal" | Plan or amount missing | Fill both |
| "Tenant workspace not found" | Workspace removed | Refresh |
| "Failed to process subscription renewal" | General failure | Retry; check logs |
| "Failed to update subscription lifecycle" | General failure | Retry; check numbers |
| "No subscriptions match the selected criteria." | Filters too narrow | Clear filters |

---

title: Payments and Invoices
content:
# Payments and Invoices
## 8.1 Purpose

A ledger of every subscription payment recorded on the platform, with total revenue, plus a form to record new payments (for example bank wires) and issue invoice entries.

## 8.2 How to get there and who can use it

Sidebar > **Payments & Invoices** (tag "Ledger"). Allowed roles: **Super Admin, Support Agent** (view). **Record Payment Entry** button: **Super Admin only** in the portal.

## 8.3 Is there payment verification or approval?

**No.** The portal has no "pending approval", "verify" or "reject" step for payments. Every payment you record, by Record Payment Entry or by Quick Renew, is saved immediately with status **paid** and the workspace is set to Active at once. Because there is no approval step, always check the money has really arrived **before** recording it.

The ledger can display the statuses PAID, PENDING, FAILED and REFUNDED, and you can filter by them, but the portal has no button to mark a payment pending, failed or refunded. Entries created in the portal are always "paid".

## 8.4 Summary cards

| Card | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Total SaaS Revenue | Sum of amounts of all **paid** entries that match the current search and status filter. Shown with a "$" sign. Amounts in different currencies are added together without conversion |
| Invoices Recorded | Number of ledger entries that match the current filter |
| Zero-PII Protection | "Ledger Only (No Bank Cards / PII)" |

## 8.5 Search and filter

| Control | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Search ("Search invoice number, workspace name, or transaction ref...") | Part of invoice number, workspace name or transaction reference. Press Enter |
| Status dropdown | All Statuses, Paid, Pending, Failed, Refunded |
| Refresh icon | Reloads |

## 8.6 Table columns

| Column | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Invoice # | Invoice number and internal record ID |
| Workspace | Name and workspace ID |
| Plan & Amount | Currency and amount, plan name and billing cycle |
| Billing Period | Start date - end date |
| Method & Ref | Payment method, "Ref:" transaction reference, and notes in quotes |
| Status | PAID, PENDING, FAILED or the raw status text |
| Recorded Date | Date and "By: <staff name>" (shows "System" when no staff is recorded) |

## 8.7 Record Payment Entry (Super Admin)

Pop-up "Record Subscription Payment": "Generate an official invoice entry and extend tenant subscription validity."

| Field | Required | Details |
|---|---|---|
| Target Workspace | Yes | Dropdown showing name, plan and status. Only the first 100 workspaces are listed |
| Subscription Tier | Yes | Plan with prices. Picking a plan fills the Amount from its price for the chosen cycle |
| Cycle | - | Monthly (+30 Days), Yearly (+365 Days), Custom Duration. Choosing Monthly sets Duration to 30, Yearly to 365 |
| Duration (Days) | Yes | Whole number, minimum 1. Edit it for custom periods |
| Amount Paid | Yes | 0 or more, 2 decimals |
| Currency | Yes | Typed in capitals, default USD |
| Method | - | Stripe, Razorpay, Bank Wire / Transfer, Corporate Credit Card, Manual Cash / Override, Cryptocurrency |
| Transaction Ref | No | e.g. "WIRE-88392-NY". Searchable later |
| Internal Notes | No | Free text |
| Send invoice receipt email to workspace owner immediately | Checkbox, on | Emails owner if one exists |
| Record & Issue Invoice | Button | "Recording..." while saving |

What recording does:

- Creates the ledger entry (status **paid**) with a new invoice number.
- Period start is now; period end is now + **Duration (Days)**.
- Sets the workspace to the chosen plan, status **Active**, expiry = period end, and resets the four limits to that plan's standard values (overwriting custom limits).
- Stores your name as the person who recorded it.
- Audit entry: `payment.record_entry`.

## 8.8 Step-by-step: record a bank-wire payment

1. Confirm in your bank records that the money has arrived.
2. Open **Payments & Invoices** and click **Record Payment Entry**.
3. Choose the **Target Workspace**.
4. Choose the **Subscription Tier** (amount fills in; correct it if the customer paid a different amount).
5. Choose **Cycle** and check **Duration (Days)**.
6. Set **Method** to Bank Wire / Transfer and enter the bank reference in **Transaction Ref**.
7. Keep the receipt email ticked if the customer should get an invoice email.
8. Click **Record & Issue Invoice**.
9. The new entry appears at the top. The workspace is now Active until the new expiry date.

## 8.9 Notes and limits of this screen

- Only the first 100 workspaces appear in the Target Workspace list. If a workspace is missing, use **Subscriptions > Quick Renew** instead.
- There is no edit or delete for ledger entries and no refund button. Correct mistakes by speaking to your Super Admin and your engineering team, and add a note to the ticket or record.
- Receipt emails go to the workspace owner's email. The owner's email is not displayed in the portal.
- Ten entries per page.

## 8.10 Common errors

| Message | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "tenantId, planId, and amount are required" | Missing workspace, plan or amount | Complete the form |
| "Tenant workspace not found" | Workspace no longer exists | Refresh the page |
| "Failed to record payment transaction" | General failure | Retry; check System Logs |
| "No payment records found." | Nothing matches | Clear filters |

---

title: Support Helpdesk
content:
# Support Helpdesk
## 9.1 Purpose

Answer support tickets raised by customers from inside their workspace. You can reply to the customer, write private internal notes visible only to staff, and set status, priority and assignee.

## 9.2 How to get there and who can use it

Sidebar > **Support Helpdesk** (tag "Cases"). Allowed roles: **Super Admin, Support Agent**.

## 9.3 Screen layout

- Title "Platform Support & Helpdesk" and a **Refresh Tickets** icon.
- Six **stat chips**.
- Left: ticket list with search and three filters.
- Right: the open ticket (appears when you click a ticket).

New tickets, new messages and changes made by other staff **appear automatically** without refreshing.

## 9.4 Stat chips

| Chip | Counts |
|---|---|
| Open | Tickets with status Open |
| In Progress | Tickets with status In Progress |
| Pending User | Tickets waiting for the customer |
| Urgent | Urgent tickets that are not Resolved or Closed |
| Unassigned | Tickets with no assignee that are not Resolved or Closed |
| Resolved | Tickets that are Resolved **or** Closed |

## 9.5 Ticket list: search and filters

| Control | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Search ("Search ticket #, subject, tenant...") | Matches ticket number, subject, the customer's email, or workspace name. Press Enter |
| All Statuses | Open, In Progress, Pending User, Resolved, Closed |
| All Priorities | Urgent, High, Medium, Low |
| All Categories | Billing, Technical, Channels, Account, Feature, General |

The list is sorted with **Urgent first, then High, Medium, Low**, and within each priority by most recent activity. 15 tickets per page. Each card shows ticket number, priority badge, status badge, subject, workspace name and customer name, last activity date, category and assignee ("Unassigned" if none).

## 9.6 Ticket statuses and what they mean

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Open | New or reopened; nobody has answered yet |
| In Progress | Staff are working on it |
| Pending Customer ("Pending User") | Waiting for the customer to reply |
| Resolved | Staff consider it solved. The customer receives a "ticket resolved" email the first time you set this |
| Closed | Finished. Counts together with Resolved in the stat chip |

Automatic status changes:

- When staff send a **public reply** to an **Open** ticket, it moves to **In Progress**.
- When a **customer replies** to a **Resolved** or **Closed** ticket, it reopens as **Open**.
- Internal notes never change the status.
- The portal does not force an order (you can move between any statuses). Setting Resolved stamps a "resolved at" time; Closed stamps a "closed at" time.

## 9.7 Priorities and categories

| Priorities | Urgent, High, Medium, Low (customers start at Medium unless they choose otherwise) |
|---|---|
| Categories | Billing, Technical, Channels (channel integration), Account, Feature (feature request), General |

You can change priority from the ticket panel. Category appears on the cards and can be filtered; the ticket panel does not have a category selector.

## 9.8 The ticket panel

| Element | Details |
|---|---|
| Header | Ticket number, priority badge, status badge, **X** to close the panel, subject |
| **Status** dropdown | Open, In Progress, Pending Customer, Resolved, Closed. Applies immediately on change |
| **Priority** dropdown | Urgent, High, Medium, Low. Applies immediately |
| **Assignee** dropdown | "Unassigned" or a staff member shown as "Name (role)". Applies immediately |
| Customer card | Customer name, email, and workspace |
| Conversation | Customer messages (cyan "CUSTOMER") and staff replies (indigo "SUPPORT AGENT"), oldest first. Internal notes appear in an amber box labelled "Internal Staff Note • <name>" with "Hidden from customer view" |
| Reply box | Two mode buttons (see 9.10), message box, **Mark as Resolved** (shown unless already Resolved), and send button |

## 9.9 Step-by-step: take ownership of a ticket

1. Open **Support Helpdesk**.
2. Click a ticket card (use the **Unassigned** chip or filters to find unowned tickets).
3. In **Assignee**, choose your name.
4. Set **Status** to In Progress if you are starting work.
5. Set **Priority** if it should change.

> **Good to know:** ** The Assignee list is loaded from the staff list, which only **Super Admins** are allowed to read. For a **Support Agent**, the list can come back empty, so only "Unassigned" is offered. If that happens, ask a Super Admin to assign tickets for you. Assignment errors are not shown on screen.

## 9.10 Step-by-step: reply to the customer

1. Open the ticket.
2. Make sure the mode button **Public Customer Reply (Email Dispatched)** is selected (indigo).
3. Type your reply (the box requires text; blank or spaces-only is refused).
4. Click **Send Customer Reply** ("Sending..." shows).
5. The customer receives your reply by **email and in the workspace app**. The ticket moves to In Progress if it was Open.
6. If this answers the issue, click **Mark as Resolved**. The customer gets a resolved notification email.

## 9.11 Step-by-step: write an internal note

1. Open the ticket.
2. Click **Staff Only Internal Note** (turns amber).
3. Type the note.
4. Click **Save Internal Note**.
5. The note is visible to platform staff only. Customers never see it. No email is sent and the status does not change.

## 9.12 Step-by-step: wait for the customer

1. Reply publicly asking for the information.
2. Set **Status** to **Pending Customer**.
3. When the customer replies, the ticket updates automatically.

## 9.13 Privacy and conduct

- Ticket text comes from the customer. Do not copy it outside the helpdesk.
- You never need to access the customer's workspace; ask them for what you need in the ticket.
- Do not ask customers to send passwords or card numbers.
- Replies, notes and changes are recorded in the Audit Trail as `support.post_public_reply`, `support.add_internal_note` and `support.update_ticket` (the audit records the length of the message, not its text).

## 9.14 Common errors

| Message / symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Message text cannot be blank" | Empty reply | Type a message |
| "Failed to post message to ticket thread" | General failure | Retry; the text stays in the box |
| "Support ticket not found" | Ticket removed | Refresh the list |
| Changing status/priority/assignee seems to do nothing | The change failed. Errors on these three dropdowns are not displayed | Refresh and try again; check System Logs; confirm you are Super Admin or Support Agent |
| Assignee list only shows "Unassigned" | Support Agents cannot read the staff list | Ask a Super Admin |
| "No support cases matching criteria." | Filters too narrow | Clear filters |
| New messages do not appear by themselves | Live connection dropped | Click Refresh Tickets |

---

title: Infra Telemetry
content:
# Infra Telemetry
## 10.1 Purpose

A live view of the health of the platform's servers: database, cache, real-time connections, memory and host details, plus last-24-hour anomaly counts.

## 10.2 How to get there and who can use it

Sidebar > **Infra Telemetry** (tag "Live"). Allowed roles: **Super Admin, Platform Dev**. Title: "Infrastructure & Process Telemetry" with a "LIVE METRICS" tag.

## 10.3 Controls

| Control | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Auto-Refresh (5s) checkbox | On by default; reloads every 5 seconds |
| Poll Now | Reloads immediately |
| "Last telemetry snapshot: <time>" | Bottom of page; the time of the last successful load |

## 10.4 The four live cards

| Card | What it shows | How to read it |
|---|---|---|
| POSTGRES POOL (database) | Status label, response time in ms ("latency"), connections: Active, Idle, Waiting | **healthy** = answering. If unreachable the latency is shown as -1ms. A rising **Waiting** number means requests are queuing for a database connection |
| REDIS PUB/SUB CLUSTER | Status label, ping time ("Fallback" when no ping is available), State: Connected or In-Memory | "In-Memory" means the cache service is not connected and the platform is running on its built-in fallback |
| REAL-TIME WEBSOCKETS | Number of connected clients and number of active workspaces | Live connections from customer apps |
| NODE.JS HEAP USED | Memory in use / total heap, plus RSS and external memory, and the process ID (PID) | Steady growth over hours may indicate a memory problem |

Status labels shown are: for the database **healthy**, **degraded** or **unreachable**; for Redis **healthy**, **degraded** or **unreachable**.

> **Good to know:** ** The real-time card always shows the label "ACTIVE" and the text "Port: 4000" as fixed text; it is not a health check.

## 10.5 Host Server Environment panel

| Item | Meaning |
|---|---|
| NODE RUNTIME | Version of the server software |
| OS PLATFORM / ARCH | Operating system and processor type |
| CPU CORES | Number of processor cores |
| LOAD AVERAGE (1/5/15m) | Average server load over 1, 5 and 15 minutes. Values consistently above the core count suggest overload. (Often 0 on Windows hosts.) |
| SYSTEM MEMORY | Free / total memory in MB |
| PROCESS UPTIME | How long the application process has been running (days, hours, minutes, seconds) |

## 10.6 24h Anomaly & Platform Activity panel

| Item | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Webhook Delivery Failures (24h) | Number of outgoing customer webhook deliveries that failed in the last 24 hours (external endpoint returning errors or timing out). Shown 0 if the figure cannot be read |
| Top Administrative Actions (24h) | The ten most frequent staff actions in the last 24 hours with counts, or "No administrative operations recorded in the last 24 hours." |

## 10.7 Step-by-step: check platform health

1. Open **Infra Telemetry**.
2. Confirm the database card says **healthy** and latency is low.
3. Confirm Redis is **Connected** (or know that In-Memory is intentional).
4. Check **Waiting** connections is 0 or very low.
5. Check heap usage is not close to total.
6. Check Webhook Delivery Failures for spikes.
7. If something looks wrong, open **System Logs** (section 11) and filter by module (for example PostgreSQL & Redis).

## 10.8 Common problems

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Page stays on "Loading live telemetry feeds..." | Server not reachable or your session expired | Refresh; sign in again |
| Database shows unreachable | Database down or unreachable | Escalate to engineering immediately |
| Numbers freeze | Auto-Refresh off or connection lost | Tick Auto-Refresh or press Poll Now |

---

title: System Logs
content:
# System Logs
## 11.1 Purpose

A live log viewer for the application. It shows recent log lines and detailed error traces, filterable by workspace, level, module and keyword. Use it to investigate a customer problem by Request ID or workspace.

## 11.2 How to get there and who can use it

Sidebar > **System Logs** (tag "Stream"). Title "System Telemetry & Workspace Logs". Allowed roles: **Super Admin, Platform Dev, Support Agent**. Download and Clear buttons: **Super Admin and Platform Dev only**.

## 11.3 What the logs are

- The live view reads a **memory buffer** (a rolling window of the most recent entries held by the running server), not a permanent archive. Older entries drop out, and restarting the server empties the buffer.
- Permanent files (`app.log`, `error.log`) are on the server disk and can be downloaded by Super Admins and Platform Devs.
- Logs are described as data-blind: operational details, not customer messages.

## 11.4 Toolbar

| Control | Visible to | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| Refresh | All | Reloads now |
| app.log / error.log (download) | Super Admin, Platform Dev | Opens the download of the full file from the server disk in a new browser tab |
| Clear Buffer | Super Admin, Platform Dev | Asks "Are you sure you want to clear the in-memory log buffer? This action is audited." Clears both the live log buffer and the error buffer **for everyone**. Shows a green or red result message with a **Dismiss** button |
| Stream Rate | All | Paused (Manual), 2 seconds (Real-time), 5 seconds (Normal, default), 10 seconds (Slow), 30 seconds |

## 11.5 Tabs

| Tab | Shows |
|---|---|
| **Live Stream (n)** | Recent log lines, newest first. Up to 200 entries are displayed (the server's cap is 1000 but the portal requests 200) |
| **Error Stack Traces (n)** | Recent errors with stack traces, newest first, up to 100 entries |

The number in brackets is the total matching entries in the buffer for the active tab.

## 11.6 Filters

| Filter | Tab | Options |
|---|---|---|
| Filter by Workspace Tenant | Both | "All Workspaces (Global Platform Stream)" or one workspace (list shows name, first 8 characters of ID and plan; first 100 workspaces) |
| Log Level | Live Stream only | All Levels, INFO, WARN, ERROR, DEBUG |
| Subsystem Module | Live Stream only | All Modules, HTTP Gateway, Auth & Session, Inbound Webhooks, Flow Execution Engine, AI Copilot & RAG, PostgreSQL & Redis, Platform Governance |
| Search Keywords / Req ID | Both | Searches message text, request ID, workspace ID, error message and stack trace. An **X** clears the box |

Filters apply as you change them; the search box applies as you type.

## 11.7 Reading a log line

Each line shows: time (hours:minutes:seconds.milliseconds, UTC), a level badge, the module in brackets, the message, and (for errors) the first 3 lines of the stack trace. On the right: duration in ms, an HTTP status chip (green below 400, amber 400-499, red 500 and above), a short workspace tag (`t:` and 6 characters) and a short request ID (`req:` and 6 characters) that you can click to **copy the full request ID**.

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| INFO (blue) | Normal events |
| WARN (amber) | Unusual but handled |
| ERROR (red) | Something failed |
| DEBUG (grey) | Detailed diagnostics |

Click any line to open the **Telemetry Entry Details** pop-up: Message, Timestamp, Module, Tenant Workspace ("Global / Internal" if none), Request ID, full Exception & Stack Trace, and Structured Metadata. **Copy Raw JSON** copies the entry. Click outside the pop-up or the **X** to close.

## 11.8 Step-by-step: investigate a customer-reported error

1. Ask the customer (via the ticket) roughly when it happened and what they were doing.
2. Open **System Logs**.
3. Pick the customer's workspace in **Filter by Workspace Tenant**.
4. Open the **Error Stack Traces** tab.
5. Look for entries around the reported time. Click one to see full detail.
6. Copy the Request ID and search for it on the **Live Stream** tab to see everything that happened in that request.
7. Describe findings in a ticket **internal note** (do not paste anything sensitive in a public reply).
8. For anything needing a code fix, hand over the Request ID and timestamp to engineering.

## 11.9 Common problems

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "No matching log entries found" | Filters too narrow, buffer was cleared, or the server restarted | Widen filters; try later; ask for file logs |
| Old entries are missing | The buffer only holds recent entries | Download file logs (Super Admin / Dev) |
| Stream not updating | Stream Rate set to "Paused (Manual)" | Choose a rate or click Refresh |
| Clear Buffer error "Failed to clear logs" | Permission or server issue | Check your role; retry |

---

title: Testing Suite
content:
# Testing Suite
## 12.1 Purpose

Safe, **dry-run** tools for testers and developers: build a sample inbound webhook message for a channel type, and count active channels by type across the platform. Nothing is stored in any customer inbox.

## 12.2 How to get there and who can use it

Sidebar > **Testing Suite** (tag "QA"). Title "Platform Synthetic Testing Suite" with a "SANDBOX UTILITIES" tag. Allowed roles: **Super Admin, Platform Dev, QA / Tester**.

## 12.3 Synthetic Inbound Webhook Dispatcher

| Field | Details |
|---|---|
| Target Ingestion Channel | Three buttons: **WhatsApp Cloud**, **Telegram Bot**, **Web Live Chat** (default WhatsApp Cloud) |
| Mock Sender Identifier | Default "+15550009999". For WhatsApp the leading "+" is removed in the sample |
| Mock Message Payload Text | Default "Hello from synthetic QA dispatcher" |
| Dispatch Dry-Run Webhook | Button ("Executing Synthetic Dispatch..." while running) |

No field is mandatory; blank values fall back to defaults on the server.

**Execution Output & Pipeline Metrics** panel (right side) shows, after a run:

- A header chip "HTTP 200 OK (N ms)".
- A green line: "Synthetic webhook verification verified successfully (Dry-run mode)."
- The **Simulated Payload Dispatched** (the sample message data, formatted).

A hint under the form says dry-run tests simulate the webhook signature calculation and payload parsing without saving to customer inboxes.

Every dispatch is recorded in the Audit Trail as `test.webhook_dispatch`.

## 12.4 Platform Channel Health Diagnostic

Click **Execute Channel Health Audit** ("Scanning..." shows). Results:

| Item | Meaning |
|---|---|
| AGGREGATE STATUS | "ok", "degraded" or "error". Currently the check returns "ok" whenever the count query completes |
| Scan Latency | Time the scan took in ms |
| ACTIVE CHANNELS | Total active channels across all workspaces |
| CHANNELS BY CONNECTOR TYPE | A count for each connector type (for example whatsapp, telegram, web) |

> **Good to know:** ** This audit counts channels that are marked active in the database. It does **not** contact WhatsApp, Telegram or any outside service, so it cannot tell you whether a channel can actually send or receive.

## 12.5 Step-by-step: run a dry-run webhook test

1. Open **Testing Suite**.
2. Choose the channel button.
3. Optionally change the sender and text.
4. Click **Dispatch Dry-Run Webhook**.
5. Read the output panel. Copy the payload if you need it for a developer.

## 12.6 Common problems

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Nothing appears after clicking Dispatch | The call failed (no on-screen error) | Retry; check your session; see System Logs |
| "Insufficient platform permissions..." in logs | Role not allowed | Use a Super Admin, Dev or Tester account |
| Channel audit says Click "Execute Channel Health Audit" | You have not run it yet | Click the button |

---

title: Staff and RBAC
content:
# Staff and RBAC
## 13.1 Purpose

Create platform staff accounts, set each person's role, and suspend or deactivate access.

## 13.2 How to get there and who can use it

Sidebar > **Staff & RBAC**. Title "Platform Staff & RBAC" with a "SUPER ADMIN GOVERNANCE" tag. Allowed role: **Super Admin only**.

## 13.3 Role description cards

Four cards at the top describe each role:

| Role | Card description |
|---|---|
| super_admin | Full platform governance, staff user lifecycle, tenant suspension and quota overrides, and audit log inspection |
| platform_dev | Live process telemetry, database pool metrics, Redis latency, WebSocket connection stats, and system error analysis |
| platform_tester | Synthetic webhook ingestion testing, dry-run channel dispatch, and connectivity diagnostic sweeps |
| support_agent | Read-only metadata verification, tenant workspace status checks, and quota troubleshooting (Zero-PII shield enforced) |

> **Good to know:** ** The Support Agent card says "read-only", but in practice Support Agents can also renew subscriptions, edit subscription limits and status, and work tickets (see section 2.2). Use section 2 of this manual as the accurate permission list.

## 13.4 Staff table ("Active Platform Personnel")

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Operator Name & Email | Name and email |
| Assigned Role | Role code in a coloured tag |
| Security & MFA | "MFA Enforced" or "Standard Auth" (reads a stored flag; the portal has no screen to change it) |
| Account Status | ACTIVE (green), SUSPENDED (amber), DEACTIVATED (red) |
| Last Active | Last sign-in date and time, or "Never logged in" |
| Actions | **Modify Access** |

A counter shows "Total: N staff". All statuses are listed, including suspended and deactivated people. The list is newest account first.

## 13.5 Account statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Active (Full Clearance) | Can sign in and use the portal |
| Suspended (Temporary Revocation) | Cannot sign in; existing sessions stop working at the next request |
| Deactivated (Terminated Access) | Cannot sign in; used when someone leaves |

## 13.6 Create Platform Operator

Button **Create Platform Operator** opens the pop-up.

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| Operator Full Name | Yes | Text |
| Platform Staff Email | Yes | Valid email format. Must be unique (not case-sensitive) |
| Temporary Staff Password | Yes | The portal does not enforce a length or complexity rule here. Choose at least 10 characters (the minimum used when staff change their own password) and share it securely |
| Assigned Platform Role | Yes | Support Agent (default), Platform QA / Tester, Platform Dev, Super Admin |

Click **Provision Staff Account** ("Provisioning..."). New accounts start **Active**. Audit entry: `staff.create` (records email and role, never the password).

## 13.7 Step-by-step: add a new staff member

1. Open **Staff & RBAC**.
2. Click **Create Platform Operator**.
3. Enter name, email, a temporary password and the **least powerful role** that lets the person do their job.
4. Click **Provision Staff Account**.
5. Share the sign-in address and temporary password through a secure channel.
6. Check the person appears in the table.

## 13.8 Modify Access

Click **Modify Access** on a row. The pop-up "Modify Staff Clearance" shows name and email, and two fields:

| Field | Options |
|---|---|
| Platform Role | Support Agent, Platform QA / Tester, Platform Dev, Super Admin |
| Account Lifecycle Status | Active, Suspended, Deactivated |

Click **Save Staff Privileges** ("Saving Changes..."). Audit entry: `staff.update`. Role changes apply to screens immediately on the person's next page load or request.

## 13.9 Step-by-step: remove someone's access

1. Click **Modify Access** on their row.
2. Set **Account Lifecycle Status** to **Deactivated** (or **Suspended** if temporary).
3. Click **Save Staff Privileges**.
4. Their next request is refused.

## 13.10 Safety guidance

- Keep the number of Super Admins small.
- There is **no safeguard** in the portal against a Super Admin changing their own role or suspending themselves. Be careful not to lock the last Super Admin out.
- The portal cannot change a staff member's name, email or password, or delete accounts. Deactivate instead of deleting.

## 13.11 Common errors

| Message | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "email, password, name, and role are required" | A field was empty | Complete the form |
| "A platform user with this email already exists" | Duplicate email | Use another email or edit the existing account |
| "Platform staff member not found" | Account removed | Refresh |
| "Failed to create platform staff member" / "Failed to update platform staff member" | General failure | Retry |
| "Insufficient platform permissions..." | You are not a Super Admin | Ask a Super Admin |

---

title: Platform Audit Trail
content:
# Platform Audit Trail
## 14.1 Purpose

A permanent record of administrative and security actions taken by platform staff. Use it to answer "who changed this, and when?"

## 14.2 How to get there and who can use it

Sidebar > **Platform Audit Trail**. Title "Platform Audit Trail" with an "IMMUTABLE LOGS" tag. Allowed roles: **Super Admin, Platform Dev, Support Agent**. The trail is read-only; entries cannot be edited or deleted from the portal.

## 14.3 Filters

| Control | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Workspace Filter | "All Workspaces (Global)" or one workspace (list shows name and first 8 characters of ID; first 100 workspaces). Applies immediately. Matches entries whose target or recorded details point at that workspace |
| Action Type / Keyword | Type an action name, then click **Filter** (or press Enter) |
| Refresh Trail | Reloads |

> **Good to know:** **
- The action box is described as a keyword search but the server matches the **exact** action name (for example `plan.update`). A partial word such as "plan" returns nothing. Use the action names in 14.6.
- The portal shows the **latest 100 entries** (the server allows at most 200).
- The newest entry is selected automatically.

## 14.4 Event table

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Timestamp | **Time only** (hours:minutes:seconds). Use the inspector for the full date |
| Staff Operator | Email of the staff member ("System" if none) |
| Action Type | Colour-coded action name |
| Target | Kind of item and its ID, for example `tenant_subscription:<workspace id>` |
| Details | Arrow icon; click the row to inspect |

Footer: "Total Entries: N" (the number loaded, up to 100).

Colours: red for actions containing suspend, delete, deactivate or clear; green for create or activate; amber for test or synthetic; cyan for auth or login; indigo for everything else.

## 14.5 Audit Payload Inspector

Click a row to see, on the right: Event ID, Operator email, Client IP ("Internal/Local" if unknown), full Timestamp (international format, UTC), and **Structured Details & State Delta** (the recorded details such as plan name, new status, invoice number).

## 14.6 Actions recorded

| Action name | Triggered when |
|---|---|
| `staff.login` | A staff member signs in successfully (failed attempts are not recorded here) |
| `staff.create` | A staff account is created |
| `staff.update` | A staff role/status is changed |
| `plan.create` | A plan tier is created |
| `plan.update` | A plan tier is edited |
| `plan.delete` | A plan tier is deleted |
| `plan.deactivate` | A plan tier in use is deactivated instead of deleted |
| `subscription.lifecycle_update` | Plan/status/expiry/limits edited on Subscriptions (and on the Govern pop-up) |
| `subscription.renew` | Quick Renew |
| `payment.record_entry` | Record Payment Entry |
| `tenant.governance_update` | Recorded by the older tenant-governance service; the Govern pop-up currently uses the subscription update, so expect `subscription.lifecycle_update` for it |
| `support.post_public_reply` | A public ticket reply is sent |
| `support.add_internal_note` | An internal note is added |
| `support.update_ticket` | Ticket status, priority, category or assignee changed |
| `telemetry.logs_cleared` | Log buffer cleared |
| `test.webhook_dispatch` | Synthetic webhook test run |

Viewing screens is not recorded.

## 14.7 Step-by-step: find who suspended a workspace

1. Open **Platform Audit Trail**.
2. In **Workspace Filter**, choose the workspace.
3. Type `subscription.lifecycle_update` in **Action Type / Keyword** and click **Filter**.
4. Click the entries and read the details (they show the status chosen).

## 14.8 Common problems

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "No audit log records found matching the filter." | Exact action name not matched, or no events | Clear the action box; check spelling |
| Cannot see the date | Table shows time only | Click the row and read Timestamp in the inspector |

title: Common tasks (quick recipes)
content:
# Common tasks (quick recipes)
| I need to... | Go to | Steps in short |
|---|---|---|
| Find a workspace and see its usage | Tenant Workspaces | Search by name/ID; read channels, seats, message bar |
| Suspend a workspace | Tenant Workspaces (Super Admin) or Subscriptions | Govern/pencil > Status = Suspended > Save |
| Reactivate a workspace | Same | Status = Active and a valid expiry date > Save |
| Give extra channels or messages to one workspace | Subscriptions > pencil | Edit the limit fields > Save (do not use -1) |
| Renew after a customer paid | Subscriptions > Quick Renew | Check amount and method > Confirm |
| Record a bank wire | Payments & Invoices (Super Admin) | Record Payment Entry |
| Check revenue | Payments & Invoices | Read Total SaaS Revenue; filter as needed |
| Create a new plan | SaaS Plan Tiers (Super Admin) | Create Plan Tier |
| Stop offering a plan | SaaS Plan Tiers | Trash icon (or untick Active Tier) |
| Answer a customer | Support Helpdesk | Open ticket > Public Customer Reply |
| Discuss internally | Support Helpdesk | Staff Only Internal Note |
| Check if servers are healthy | Infra Telemetry | Read the four cards |
| Trace a customer's error | System Logs | Filter by workspace; Error Stack Traces |
| Add a colleague | Staff & RBAC (Super Admin) | Create Platform Operator |
| Remove a leaver | Staff & RBAC | Modify Access > Deactivated |
| See who changed something | Platform Audit Trail | Filter by workspace and exact action |

title: Common errors and fixes (portal-wide)
content:
# Common errors and fixes (portal-wide)
| What you see | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Sent to the sign-in page unexpectedly | Session expired (24 hours) or your account was changed | Sign in again |
| "Platform authentication required: Missing bearer token" | Request sent without a sign-in | Sign in again |
| "Invalid or expired platform token" | Session no longer valid | Sign in again |
| "Platform staff account no longer exists." | Your account was removed | Contact a Super Admin |
| "Platform staff account is suspended/deactivated. Access denied." | Account status changed | Contact a Super Admin |
| "Insufficient platform permissions. Required one of: [...], but you have role '...'." | Your role is not allowed for that action | Ask a Super Admin, or use the right account |
| "Platform Access Restricted" page | You opened a screen not allowed for your role | Click Return to Permitted View |
| "HTTP 500: ..." or a generic failure message | Server problem | Retry once; then report to engineering with the time and, if possible, the Request ID from System Logs |
| A list says "Loading ..." for a long time | Server slow or unreachable | Refresh; check Infra Telemetry |
| Data on screen looks stale | Auto-refresh is off or you are on a screen without live updates | Use the Refresh button |
| A save button is greyed out | A save is in progress, or the Govern pop-up is still loading | Wait a moment |
| Button missing that a colleague has | Buttons depend on role | See section 2.2 |

Screens that show **no** visible error on failure (they only log in the browser): the tenant list, plan list, subscription list, payment ledger, staff list, ticket list, ticket status/priority/assignee changes, telemetry, logs, audit, and the testing tools. If a screen is empty or a change does not stick, press Refresh and try again before assuming the action worked.

title: Glossary
content:
# Glossary
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Tenant / Workspace | A customer account on the platform |
| Plan tier | A pricing and limits package (for example Starter) |
| Entitlement / Quota | A limit: channels, contacts, messages per month, AI queries per month |
| Lifecycle | The subscription's status and expiry over time |
| Quick Renew | Records a paid renewal and extends access |
| Ledger | The list of recorded payments and invoices |
| Invoice number | Unique reference like `INV-202610-0001-4821` |
| Channel | A connected messaging channel such as WhatsApp, Telegram or web chat |
| Privacy Shield | The rule that staff screens never expose customer conversations, contacts or payment credentials |
| Zero-PII | No personal data of the customer's end users |
| Internal note | A ticket note only staff can see |
| Request ID | A short code attached to every server request, used to trace it in logs |
| Telemetry | Live technical health measurements |
| Dry run | A test that does not change or send real customer data |
| RBAC | Role-based access control: what you can do depends on your role |
